record.title: Andrews–Garvan–Straub conjecture on linear congruences for the function $\xi(n)$
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $\xi(n)$ denote the function studied in the paper, and let $A,n\in\mathbb N$. 

**Andrews–Garvan–Straub conjecture.** There exists a $B\in\mathbb N$ such that

$$
\xi\left(p^A n-B\right)\equiv0\pmod{p^A}
$$

for all $n$ precisely when

$$
p=23\quad\text{or}\quad p\equiv 5,7,10,11,14,15,17,19,20,21,22\pmod {23}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the congruences already exhibited for $\xi(n)$ account for all linear congruences of the indicated form. The source describes it as an important challenge for future work, and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Pavel Guerzhoy, Zachary Kent and Larry Rolen, “Congruences for Taylor expansions of quantum modular forms”, arXiv:1411.1047 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.1047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

record.title: Existence conjecture for type I(b) solutions
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime. A solution is called a type I(b) solution when

$$
x=\left\lfloor\frac{py}{4y-p}\right\rfloor+1.
$$

**Type I(b) existence conjecture.** Every prime $p$ has a type I(b) solution.

The conjecture is supported by computation through all primes less than $10^8$. The paper notes that the prime $p=193$ has a type I(b) solution even though it has no type I(a) solution, so the claim is stronger than the preceding exceptional-prime statement.
record.source_name: Kyle Bradford and Eugen Ionascu, “A Geometric Consideration of the Erdős-Straus Conjecture”, arXiv:1411.3403 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.3403

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

record.title: Frobenius-series conjecture for the degree-three monomial family
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_3$ be the family of all monomials of total degree $3$ in $x_{11},\ldots,x_{1n}$, and let $\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{T}_3}$ be its associated polarization module. **Frobenius-series conjecture.** Its graded Frobenius characteristic is given by the table in the source, with the displayed formulas for $n=1,2,3,4,5$ and for all $n\geq6$. The conjecture was verified in the paper up to $n=6$ and $\ell=3$, but the supplied statement does not reproduce the table itself.
record.source_name: Hector Blandin, “Generalized Polarizations Modules (Extended Abstract)”, arXiv:1411.4197 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4197

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2014).

record.title: The alternating-diagram maximal volume conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an alternating hyperbolic knot, and let $K'$ be obtained from $K$ by changing crossings in a diagram. **The alternating-diagram maximal volume conjecture.**
(a) If any crossing of $K$ is changed, then

$$
{\rm vol}(K')<{\rm vol}(K).
$$

(b) The same inequality holds when any proper subset of crossings of $K$ is changed. The conjecture concerns whether alternating diagrams maximize hyperbolic volume among diagrams with a given projection. Part (a) has been verified for all alternating knots up to 18 crossings, while part (b) remains open; under twisting on two strands, the volume difference can nevertheless be arbitrarily small and positive.
record.source_name: Abhijit Champanerkar, Ilya Kofman and Jessica S. Purcell, “Geometrically and diagrammatically maximal knots”, arXiv:1411.7915 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.7915

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

record.title: Sum Rule II for canonical-basis component sums
record.statement:
Let $s_{m,L}$ denote the sum associated with the dual canonical bases of the tensor-product representation indexed by $m$ and of length $L$, evaluated at $q=1$. Let $c_n$ be the integer sequence A00902, specified by

$$
c_n=2c_{n-1}+(2n-2)c_{n-2},
$$

with $c_1=1$ and $c_2=3$.

**Sum Rule II.** For all $L\geq 1$,

$$
s_{1,L}=c_{L+1}.
$$

The conjecture had been checked through $L=24$ in the supplied text. It is a proposed enumeration rule relating these canonical-basis sums to the sequence A00902.
record.source_name: Keiichi Shigechi, “Canonical bases of a coideal subalgebra in U_q(sl_2)”, arXiv:1412.7285 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.7285

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

record.title: Polynomial ideal conjecture for pairwise coprime linear forms
record.statement:
Let $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathbb C[x,y]$ be linear forms such that $\gcd(f_i,f_j)=1$ for all $i\neq j$. For each pair $i<j$, let $\langle f_i+z,f_j+z\rangle$ denote the ideal of $\mathbb C[x,y,z]$ generated by $f_i+z$ and $f_j+z$. **Polynomial ideal conjecture.** One has

$$
\prod_{i=1}^m f_i\notin\bigcap_{1\leq i<j\leq m}\langle f_i+z,f_j+z\rangle.
$$

The paper states this as an equivalent commutative-algebraic formulation of the complex arrangement conjecture. It remains open in the source, although the geometric conjecture is verified there for arrangements with at most $12$ lines.
record.source_name: Benjamin Anzis and Stefan Tohaneanu, “On the geometry of real or complex supersolvable line arrangements”, arXiv:1501.04039 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.04039

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: Conjecture on an infinite family with few maximal sum-free subsets
record.statement:
Let $\mu(G)$ denote the relevant group parameter used in the paper, and let $f_{\max}(G)$ denote the number of maximal sum-free subsets of a finite abelian group $G$. **Few maximal sum-free subsets conjecture.** There is a sequence of finite abelian groups $\{G_i\}$ of increasing order such that, for every $i$,

$$
f_{\max}(G_i) \leq 2^{\mu(G_i)/2.01}.
$$

This conjecture proposes an infinite family for which the upper bounds in the preceding conjecture and in the paper’s related question are far from tight. The supplied context does not define $\mu(G)$ or give evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Hong Liu, Maryam Sharifzadeh and Andrew Treglown, “Sharp bound on the number of maximal sum-free subsets of integers”, arXiv:1502.07605 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.07605

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2015). “This conjecture was proven independently by Green and Sapozhenko .”

record.title: Zhao's log-concavity conjecture for the Fennessey-Larcombe-French sequence
record.statement:
Let $\{V_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ be the Fennessey-Larcombe-French sequence, defined by $V_0=1$, $V_1=8$, and

$$
n(n+1)^2 V_{n+1}=8n(3n^2+5n+1)V_n-128(n-1)(n+1)^2V_{n-1},\qquad n\geq 1.
$$

A sequence $\{a_n\}$ is **log-concave** when $a_n^2\geq a_{n-1}a_{n+1}$ for every relevant index. **Zhao's conjecture.** The Fennessey-Larcombe-French sequence $\{V_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ is log-concave; that is,

$$
V_n^2\geq V_{n-1}V_{n+1}\qquad(n\geq 2).
$$

The conjecture concerns the log-behavior of the sequence arising from the series expansion of the complete elliptic integral of the second kind. The paper records it after proving that $\{nV_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ and $\{V_n/(n-1)!\}_{n\geq 1}$ are log-concave; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Arthur L. B. Yang and James J. Y. Zhao, “Log-concavity of the Fennessey-Larcombe-French Sequence”, arXiv:1503.02151 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02151

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: The Hsiang conjecture on rationalized classical assembly
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a torsion-free group and $n\in\mathbb{Z}$. The rationalized classical assembly map is

$$
\bigoplus_{\substack{s+t=n\\s,t\geq0}} H_s(BG;\mathbb{Q})\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}}\bigl(K_t(\mathbb{Z})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}\bigr)\longrightarrow K_n(\mathbb{Z}G)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}.
$$

**Hsiang's conjecture.** For every torsion-free group $G$ and every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, this rationalized classical assembly map is an isomorphism.

The conjecture was formulated by Hsiang in his 1983 ICM plenary address, originally under an additional finite-classifying-space hypothesis. It is a rational form of the torsion-free assembly conjecture.
record.source_name: Wolfgang Lueck, Holger Reich, John Rognes and Marco Varisco, “Algebraic K-theory of group rings and the cyclotomic trace map”, arXiv:1504.03674 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.03674

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2015). “A well-known and still open conjecture, which we review below, predicts that the Whitehead group of any torsion-free group vanishes.”

record.title: Cao and Dehmer's monotonicity conjecture for degree-based graph entropy
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $I_{f^l_d}(G)$ denote its degree-based graph entropy as a function of the positive parameter $l$.

**Cao and Dehmer's conjecture.** For $l>0$, $I_{f^l_d}(G)$ is a monotonically increasing function of $l$ for connected graphs.

The conjecture is supported in the paper by numerical results for trees with $11$ vertices and connected graphs with $7$ vertices. Its validity for all connected graphs and all positive parameter values remains open.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Meiqin Wei, “A survey of recent results in (generalized) graph entropies”, arXiv:1505.04658 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Rank-two unit Thue inequality conjecture
record.statement:
Let $[200~s,t$ and $n$ be integers, and define

$$
F_{n,s,t}(X,Y)=(X-[201~\lambda_0^{s}\lambda_1^{t}Y)(X-\lambda_1^{s}\lambda_2^{t}Y)(X-\lambda_2^{s}\lambda_0^{t}Y).
$$

**Rank-two unit conjecture.** There exists a positive absolute constant $\kappa$ such that, whenever $n,s,t,x,y,m$ are integers satisfying

$$
\max\{|x|,|y|\}\geq 2,\qquad (s,t)\neq(0,0),\qquad 0<|F_{n,s,t}(x,y)|\leq m,
$$

then

$$
\max\{\log|n|,|s|,|t|,\log|x|,\log|y|\}\leq \kappa(1+\log m).
$$

The conjecture seeks a uniform linear bound in $1+\log m$ for all parameters and solutions of these Thue inequalities, reflecting the rank-two unit structure of the simplest cubic fields. The source does not provide a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Claude Levesque and Michel Waldschmidt, “A family of Thue equations involving powers of units of the simplest cubic fields”, arXiv:1505.06708 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06708

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: The longer-snake conjecture for Kendall snake-in-the-box codes
record.statement:
For $n\ge3$, let a $(2n+1,M_{2n+1},\mathcal{K})$-snake be a Gray code of permutations in $S_{2n+1}$ in which every two codewords have Kendall's $\tau$-distance at least two; here $\mathcal{K}$ denotes the Kendall metric.

**Longer-snake conjecture.** There exists a $(2n+1,M_{2n+1},\mathcal{K})$-snake with

$$
M_{2n+1}=\frac{(2n+1)!}{2}-2n+3
$$

for every $n\ge3$.

This would improve the previously proposed size $\frac{(2n+1)!}{2}-2n+1$; the construction is given for $S_7$ with $M_7=2517$, while feasibility for all odd dimensions remains open.
record.source_name: Yiwei Zhang and Gennian Ge, “Snake-in-the-Box Codes for Rank Modulation under Kendall's τ-Metric”, arXiv:1506.02740 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02740

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2015). “They also propose a direct construction aiming at a snake of size $\frac{(2n+1)!}{2}-2n+1$ and it is applied successfully to $S_7$ and $S_9$ via computer search.”

record.title: The non-arithmetic hyperbolic reflection group dimension conjecture
record.statement:
Let an **arithmetic hyperbolic reflection group** mean a discrete group generated by reflections in hyperbolic $n$-space whose defining quadratic form and reflection data satisfy the arithmeticity conditions used in the paper. Vinberg's theorem states that there are no arithmetic hyperbolic reflection groups in dimensions $n\geq 30$.

**Non-arithmetic dimension conjecture.** Theorem 1.1 is true without the arithmeticity assumption: there are no hyperbolic reflection groups in dimensions $n\geq 30$.

This conjecture asks whether the dimension bound known for arithmetic hyperbolic reflection groups holds for all hyperbolic reflection groups. The supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Mikhail Belolipetsky, “Arithmetic hyperbolic reflection groups”, arXiv:1506.03111 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.03111

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2015). “This conjecture can be possibly resolved by Esselmann's method , which he applied to find the maximal dimension of isotropic reflective lattices, but such a proof is not available so far.”

record.title: Baxter's stronger symmetry conjecture for hesitating walks
record.statement:
Let $a(n;i,j,m)$ denote the number of $W_2$-hesitating walks of length $2n$ from $(0,0)$ to $(i,j)$ with $m$ marked steps each leaving the diagonal $x=y$. **Baxter's stronger symmetry conjecture.** For $n,i,j\geq 0$, 
$$
a(n;i,0,j)=a(n;j,0,i).
$$
 This symmetry exchanges the endpoint coordinate and the number of marked steps. The authors state that it has been checked by recurrence computations for all $n,i,j$ with $n\leq 56$, but no general proof is given.
record.source_name: Sophie Burrill, Julien Courtiel, Eric Fusy, Stephen Melczer and Marni Mishna, “Tableau sequences, open diagrams, and Baxter families”, arXiv:1506.03544 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.03544

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

record.title: Kenyon's determinant density upper-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot or link, let $c(K)$ denote its crossing number, let $\det(K)$ denote its determinant, and let $v_{\rm oct}$ denote the volume of the regular ideal octahedron. **Kenyon's conjecture.**

$$
\frac{2\pi\log\det(K)}{c(K)} \leq v_{\rm oct}.
$$

This is equivalent to a conjecture of Kenyon for planar graphs and had been verified for all knots up to 16 crossings; its general status is not resolved in the source.
record.source_name: Abhijit Champanerkar, Ilya Kofman and Jessica S. Purcell, “Density spectra for knots”, arXiv:1506.05841 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.05841

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

record.title: Gessel's conjectured gamma-coefficient inequality
record.statement:
Let $D4AE_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $D4AE_n(231)$ be the set of permutations avoiding the pattern $231$, and let $S_n(t)$ be its descent polynomial. Write

$$
S_n(t)=\sum_k \gamma^S_{n,k}t^k(1+t)^{n-1-2k}.
$$

Let $D4AE_{n,i,j}$ be the coefficients in the expansion defining Gessel's gamma quantities. **Gessel's conjectured inequality.** For every $n$ and every $k$,

$$
\gamma_{n,k,n-1-2k}\geq \gamma^S_{n,k}.
$$

This inequality compares the gamma coefficients associated with Gessel's refinement to those of the descent polynomial on $231$-avoiding permutations. The source presents it as a conjectured inequality; its status is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Shishuo Fu, Zhicong Lin and Jiang Zeng, “On two unimodal descent polynomials”, arXiv:1507.05184 (2019).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1210.3799](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3799), [arXiv:math/0610185](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610185).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05184

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: The conjecture for the maximal dimension of constant-rank matrix spaces
record.statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $l(r;a)$ be the maximal dimension of a subspace of $a\times a$ matrices such that every nonzero matrix has rank $r$. Assume that $a$ and $r$ are integers satisfying

$$
\frac{2a+2}{3}>r>\frac{a}{2}+1.
$$

**Constant-rank matrix dimension conjecture.** Then

$$
l(r;a)=a-r+1.
$$

This conjecture is obtained by translating the uniform-bundle conjecture into the language of constant-rank matrix spaces. The paper verifies it for all $a\leq 10$, while the stated range is not settled in general.
record.source_name: Philippe Ellia and Paolo Menegatti, “Spaces of matrices of constant rank and uniform vector bundles”, arXiv:1508.00209 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.00209

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

record.title: Existence conjecture for Hadamard matrices of 2N-type
record.statement:
A **Hadamard matrix of 2N-type** is a Hadamard matrix of order $2v$ of the block form

$$
H=\left[\begin{array}{cc}A&B\\-B^T&A^T\end{array}\right],
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are negacyclic blocks. **2N-type existence conjecture.** For each even integer $v>0$, there exists a Hadamard matrix of 2N-type and order $2v$. Via the bijection between such matrices and NG-pairs, this is equivalent to the assertion that NG-pairs exist for all even lengths; the source gives no general construction and notes the absence of a pair of length $94$.
record.source_name: N. A. Balonin and D. Z. Djokovic, “Negaperiodic Golay pairs and Hadamard matrices”, arXiv:1508.00640 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.00640

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

record.title: The derangement analogue of Kurepa's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number. The relevant factorial sum is

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{p-1}j!.
$$

**Derangement factorial-sum conjecture.** For every prime number $p>11$,

$$
p\nmid\sum_{j=1}^{p-1}j!.
$$

The claim is motivated by the preceding observation relating divisibility of the infinite factorial series to its truncation and is said to resemble Kurepa's conjecture. The paper gives computations below $10^6$ consistent with the claim, but no proof.
record.source_name: Piotr Miska, “Arithmetic Properties of the Sequence of Derangements and its Generalizations”, arXiv:1508.01987 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01987

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

record.title: Recurrence relations for the remaining TRIP-Stern maximal terms
record.statement:
TRIP-Stern sequences are generated by the multidimensional continued-fraction maps associated with the permutation triplets described above, and each sequence has maximal terms indexed by $n$. The paper has explicit recurrence relations for 24 of the 120 maps and asks for the remaining 96.

**Conjectured recurrence relations.** The numerical data in the table suggest recurrence relations for the maximal terms of the TRIP-Stern sequences corresponding to the remaining 96 maps.

These conjectured recurrences extend the explicit formulas known for the other maps, but the table does not assert a single uniform recurrence or provide proofs for all 96 cases. Determining and proving the recurrence relations is posed as an open question.
record.source_name: Ilya Amburg, Krishna Dasaratha, Laure Flapan, Thomas Garrity, Chansoo Lee, Cornelia Mihaila, Nicholas Neumann-Chun, Sarah Peluse and Matthew Stoffregen, “Stern Sequences for a Family of Multidimensional Continued Fractions: TRIP-Stern Sequences”, arXiv:1509.05239 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05239

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

record.title: Weak terminal Fano volume and birationality conjectures
record.statement:
Fix an integer $n$. **Weak terminal Fano conjectures.** There exists a number $M_0(n)$ depending only on $n$ such that every $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano variety $X$ of Picard number one satisfies

$$
(-K_X)^n\leq M_0(n).
$$

There also exists an integer $r_n$ depending only on $n$ such that for every $n$-dimensional terminal Fano variety $X$, the linear system

$$
|-r_nK_X|
$$

gives a birational map. These are numerical and birational consequences expected from boundedness. The source records effective three-dimensional values $M_0(3)=64$ and $r_3=97$, while the general conjectures remain open.
record.source_name: Chen Jiang, “On birational boundedness of Fano fibrations”, arXiv:1509.08722 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.08722

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

record.title: Vanishing of higher-order degrees for complements of two transversally intersecting curves
record.statement:
Let $C$ be a curve formed by two curves that intersect transversally, and let $\delta_n$ denote the $n$-th higher-order degree of the complement of $C$. **Vanishing conjecture.** If $C$ is formed by two curves which intersect transversally, then

$$
\delta_n=0\quad\text{for all }n\geq 1.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the vanishing observed in Examples 9.9 and 9.10; its status is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Yun Su, “Higher-order Alexander Invariants of Hypersurface Complements”, arXiv:1510.03467 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.03467

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for elementary abelian class groups
record.statement: For an odd prime $p$, an **elementary abelian $p$-group** is a group isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^r$. **Nonexistence conjecture for elementary abelian class groups.** No elementary abelian $p$-group of rank at least $3$ occurs as the class group of an imaginary quadratic field. The conjecture is motivated by the observed absence of such groups in the computed tables, including $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^3$ for all odd primes $p<100$ examined in the paper. Its resolution status is not specified here.
record.source_name: Samuel Holmin, Nathan Jones, Pär Kurlberg, Cam McLeman and Kathleen L. Petersen, “Missing class groups and class number statistics for imaginary quadratic fields”, arXiv:1510.04387 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.04387

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2015). “Robert's conjecture was recently proved in .”

record.title: Small-radius convexity conjecture for Cassinian balls in the upper half-plane
record.statement: Let $\mathbb{H}^2=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$, let $\delta_{\mathbb{H}^2}(x)$ denote the Euclidean distance from $x$ to the boundary, and let $B_{c_{\mathbb{H}^2}}(x,r)$ be the Cassinian ball of radius $r$. **Small-radius convexity conjecture.** There exists $a>0$ such that $B_{c_{\mathbb{H}^2}}(x,r)$ is convex for all $x\in\mathbb{H}^2$ and $r\in(0,a\delta_{\mathbb{H}^2}(x)]$. Computer experiments suggest that this holds for $a\approx0.85$, but no proof is given.
record.source_name: Riku Klén, Manas Ranjan Mohapatra and Swadesh Kumar Sahoo, “Geometric properties of the Cassinian metric”, arXiv:1511.01298 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.01298

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: Topological invariance and existence conjecture for level-k series
record.statement: Let $K$ be a knot, let $\zeta$ be a root of unity, and let $\gamma$ be a non-degenerate Neumann–Zagier datum arising from a triangulation of the knot complement. **Topological invariance conjecture.** For every knot $K$, there exists a triangulation with a non-degenerate Neumann–Zagier datum $\gamma$. The series $\phi_{\gamma,\zeta}(\hbar)$ is independent of the choice of triangulation and $\gamma$, up to multiplication by $\zeta^{1/12}$ and $e^{\hbar/(24k)}$; modulo these ambiguities it equals $\phi_{K,\zeta}(\hbar)$, the series on the right-hand side of the Quantum Modularity Conjecture. Experimental checks for many knots and state-integral invariance motivate the claim, but the assertion is not proved in general.
record.source_name: Tudor Dimofte and Stavros Garoufalidis, “Quantum modularity and complex Chern-Simons theory”, arXiv:1511.05628 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05628

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: Zassenhaus's order conjecture for torsion units in integral group rings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Write $V(\mathbb{Z}G)$ for the group of augmentation-one units of the integral group ring, and let $u\in V(\mathbb{Z}G)$ be a torsion unit.

**Zassenhaus's order conjecture.** There exists an element $g\in G$ such that

$$
|u|=|g|.
$$

This is a basic conjecture in the theory of integral group rings. The paper's abstract states that it is proved for $PSL(2,8)$ and $PSL(2,17)$, while the assertion for arbitrary finite groups remains open.
record.source_name: Joe Gildea, “Zassenhaus Conjecture for Integral Group Rings of Simple Linear Groups”, arXiv:1512.00330 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00330

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

record.title: The update-stable zero-one conjecture for wired and free spanning forests
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an infinite network, and let $\mathfrak F$ be either the wired or free spanning forest of $G$. A Borel set $\mathscr A\subseteq \{0,1\}^E$ is **update-stable** if, for every oriented edge $e$ of $G$, the updated forest $U(\mathfrak F,e)$ belongs to $\mathscr A$ if and only if $\mathfrak F$ belongs to $\mathscr A$ almost surely.

**Update-stable zero-one conjecture.** For every update-stable Borel set $\mathscr A\subseteq \{0,1\}^E$, the probability that $\mathfrak F$ belongs to $\mathscr A$ is either zero or one.

A positive solution would yield an alternative proof that the number of excessive ends of the wired or free uniform spanning forest is nonrandom, and would also imply a positive solution to Question 15.7 of Benjamini, Lyons, Peres, and Schramm.

record.title: The exponential maximal-excursion tail control for random-environment diffusions
record.statement:
Fix $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $\omega\in\Omega$ and $n\geq 0$. For each $v\geq D_n$ and every $y$ satisfying

$$
|y-x|\leq 30\sqrt{d}L_n,
$$

**the exponential maximal-excursion tail control** asserts

$$
P_{y,\omega}(X^*_{L_n^2}\geq v)\leq \exp\left(-\frac{v}{D_n}\right).
$$

The paper notes that this estimate is not valid in general for every $(x,\omega,n)$, while related controls are available for large $n$, with high probability, on a large portion of space. The supplied text does not establish a resolution status for the displayed universal formulation.
record.source_name: Benjamin J. Fehrman, “Exit Laws of Isotropic Diffusions in Random Environment from Large Domains”, arXiv:1601.06317 (2016).

record.title: The recurrence conjecture for the q-Lommel polynomials
record.statement:
Let $r_n^{(\nu)}(x)$ be the polynomials introduced by the preceding recurrence, and let $s_n^{(\nu)}(x)$, $n\geqslant 0$, be the sequence uniquely defined by

$$
-2qx\,s_{n-1}^{(\nu)}(x)\left(q-q^{n+\nu}\right)+q^{n+\nu}s_{n-2}^{(\nu)}(x)+q^2s_n^{(\nu)}(x)=0,
$$

with initial values $s_0^{(\nu)}(x)=1$ and $s_1^{(\nu)}(x)=2x(1-q^\nu)$. **Recurrence conjecture.** For all $n\geqslant 0$,

$$
r_n^{(\nu)}(x)=s_n^{(\nu)}(x).
$$

The claim identifies the automatically guessed recurrence with the recurrence satisfied by the $q$-versions of the modified Lommel polynomials. As pointed out in Ismail (1982), it can be proved by straightforward induction.
record.source_name: Christoph Koutschan and Peter Paule, “Holonomic Tools for Basic Hypergeometric Functions”, arXiv:1602.00454 (2016).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.00454

record.title: The least square-free primitive root bound beyond 409
record.statement:
Let $g^{\square}(p)$ denote the least square-free primitive root modulo a prime $p$. **Least square-free primitive root conjecture.** For all $p>409$ we have

$$
g^{\square}(p)<\sqrt{p}-2.
$$

The preceding explicit bound proves only that $g^{\square}(p)<p^{0.96}$ for every prime $p$; this conjecture proposes a substantially stronger square-root-scale bound, motivated by computational evidence and related work.

record.title: Exponential maximal-excursion estimate for diffusions in random environments
record.statement:
Fix $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $\omega\in\Omega$, and $n\geq 0$. Let $P_{y,\omega}$ denote the law of the diffusion started at $y$ in environment $\omega$, and let $X^*_{L_n^2}$ be its maximal excursion up to time $L_n^2$. **Exponential maximal-excursion estimate.** For each $v\geq D_n$ and every $y$ satisfying

$$
|y-x|\leq 30\sqrt{d}L_n,
$$

we have

$$
P_{y,\omega}(X^*_{L_n^2}\geq v)\leq \exp\left(-\frac{v}{D_n}\right).
$$

This estimate provides the tail control needed to handle localization errors in stochastic homogenization. As with the Hölder control, the source says that it is not valid for every $(x,\omega,n)$; according to the cited result, it is available for large $n$ with high probability on a large portion of space.

record.title: The anchor-cell excess conjecture for canonical systems on metric graphs with skeleton K_4
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a metric graph whose skeleton is the complete graph $K_4$, and let $D=K$ be its canonical divisor. Write $|D|$ for the associated linear system, and call the cells in $|D|$ anchor cells and vertices in $|D|$ vertices. **Anchor-cell excess conjecture.** The number of anchor cells in $|D|$ minus the number of vertices in $|D|$ is always $16$. This is an observed computational pattern for the listed metrics on $K_4$; whether it holds for every metric on a trivalent graph with skeleton $K_4$ remains to be established.

record.title: Maeda's conjecture for cuspidal eigenforms on \(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z)\)
record.statement: We specialize to $M=1$, $K=\mathbf Q$, and trivial character. Let $P_k(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z))$ denote the set of normalized cuspidal Hecke eigenforms of weight $k$ for $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z)$, with the natural action of $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbf C)$ on their Fourier coefficients. **Maeda's conjecture.** There is only one $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbf C)$-orbit of $P_k(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z))$ for all integers $k$ with $12\le k$. This predicts that, in every weight at least $12$, all such eigenforms are Galois conjugate; the source provides no resolution status here.

record.title: Point-count conjecture for the double octic O_5
record.statement:
Let $O_5$ be the double cover of $P^3$ branched over the octic displayed in the source. For each prime $p>2$, let $a_p$ denote the eigenvalue for $T_p$ of the newform of weight $4$ and level $5$, and let $\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)$ be the Legendre symbol. **Point-count conjecture for $O_5$.** For all primes $p>2$, the threefold $O_5$ has

$$
p^3+5p^2-(9+\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right))p+1-a_p
$$

points over $F_p$. The conjecture was checked for $p<200$; the paper suggests proving it via a crepant resolution that is a rigid CalabiYau threefold, and relates it to the Tate conjecture.

record.title: Mulmuley–Sohoni padded-permanent border determinantal complexity conjecture
record.statement:
For $n>m$, let $X_{11}^{n-m}\mathrm{per}_m$ be the padded permanent, viewed as an element of $\mathsf{Sym}^n\mathbb{C}^{n^2}$, and let ${{\mathcal{D}}et}_n$ be the Euclidean (equivalently, Zariski) closure of the $\mathrm{GL}_{n^2}$-orbit of $\mathrm{det}_n$. **Mulmuley–Sohoni's border determinantal complexity conjecture.** For every $c\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge 1}$, one has

$$
X_{11}^{m^c-m}\mathrm{per}_m\notin{{\mathcal{D}}et}_{m^c}
$$

for infinitely many $m$. Membership of the padded permanent in this orbit closure would imply an upper bound on its determinantal complexity, so this conjecture would imply Valiant's determinantal complexity conjecture. It was proposed as a geometric-complexity-theory approach and remains open in the stated source context.
record.source_name: Peter Bürgisser, Christian Ikenmeyer and Greta Panova, “No occurrence obstructions in geometric complexity theory”, arXiv:1604.06431 (2018).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.06431

record.title: The major-index generating-function conjectures for rectangular posets
record.statement:
Let $EN_{s,t}(\sigma)[q]$ and $NE_{s,t}(\sigma)[q]$ denote the major-index generating functions for the indicated pattern-avoiding linear extensions of rectangular posets. Let $CW_n$ be the set of Catalan words of length $2n$, and define

$$
c_n(q)=\sum_{\pi\in CW_n}q^{\operatorname{maj}(\pi)},
$$

where $\operatorname{maj}$ is the major index. **The major-index generating-function conjectures.** For all $s\ge1$ and $t\ge1$,

$$
EN_{2,t}(321)[q]=q^t c_t(q),
$$

$$
EN_{s,2}(123)[q]=q^{2\binom{s}{2}}c_s(q),
$$

$$
NE_{s,2}(123)[q]=q^{s^2}c_s(q),
$$

$$
NE_{2,t}(123)[q]=q^{t^2}c_t(q).
$$

These four identities are presented as conjectures and were verified computationally for $s\le9$ and $t\le9$; their general validity remains open.
record.source_name: David Anderson, Eric S. Egge, Manda Riehl, Lucas Ryan, Ruth Steinke and Yuriko Vaughan, “Pattern Avoiding Linear Extensions of Rectangular Posets”, arXiv:1605.06825 (2016).

record.title: Homocyclic Sylow subgroup conjecture for irreducible p-constant characters
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $\rho$ be an irreducible $p$-constant character of $G$. Write $c_\rho$ for its constant value on the $p$-singular elements. **Homocyclic Sylow subgroup conjecture.** If $|c_\rho|>1$, then $p\neq 2$ and the Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ are homocyclic. This conjecture was verified computationally for all groups of order less than $1250$; the general classification remains open.

record.title: Yakoubov's conjecture on doubly pattern-avoiding linear extensions of alpha-labeled combs
record.statement:
Let $K_{s,2}^\alpha$ be the alpha-labeled comb with spine parameter $s$ and tooth parameter $2$, and let $A_{231,321}(K_{s,2}^\alpha)$ denote the number of its linear extensions avoiding both patterns $231$ and $321$.

**Yakoubov's conjecture.** For every integer $s\geq 1$,

$$
A_{231,321}(K_{s,2}^\alpha)=2^{s-1}(s-1)+1.
$$

The conjecture concerns the case that remained unenumerated in Yakoubov's results. The supplied text later gives a recurrence for the corresponding uneven combs, which can be used to enumerate these linear extensions, but it does not explicitly state a proof or resolution of the displayed formula.

record.title: The conjecture that the positive Pillai equation has at most two primitive solutions
record.statement:
For a positive integer $d$, consider the equation

$$
g^x+g^y=d,
$$

with integer parameters $g\geq 2$ and $1\leq x<y$. A solution is **primitive** when the relevant parameters satisfy the coprimality condition used in the paper's definition of primitive solutions. Let $N^{+}(d)$ be the number of primitive integer solutions. **Positive Pillai-solution conjecture.** For every integer $d\geq 1$, one has

$$
N^{+}(d)\leq 2.
$$

The paper reports verification for all positive integers $d\leq 10^{10}$. Under the ABC conjecture, sufficiently large $d$ satisfy the stronger bound $N^{+}(d)\leq 1$, but the stated uniform bound remains open.

record.title: The extremal $K_4$-free graph conjecture for fractional separation dimension
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph that does not contain $K_4$, and let $\pi_f(G)$ denote its fractional separation dimension. For $n\ge 10$, consider the complete tripartite graph

$$
K_{1,\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor,\lceil (n-1)/2\rceil}.
$$

**The extremal $K_4$-free graph conjecture.** For $n\ge 10$, the $n$-vertex graph not containing $K_4$ that maximizes $\pi_f$ is $K_{1,\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor,\lceil (n-1)/2\rceil}$. The conjecture is motivated by computations verifying the extremum among tripartite graphs up to $14$ vertices, while the supplied text does not establish the claim for all $n\ge 10$.

record.title: The Planar Conjecture on embedding planar graph metrics into \ell_1
record.statement: A **planar graph metric** is a shortest-path metric on a finite planar graph whose edges have arbitrary weights. **The Planar Conjecture.** Every metric supported on a finite planar graph can be embedded into $\ell_1$ with constant distortion. This is a central open problem in the theory of metric embeddings; the cited work proves the analogous statement for graphs excluding $K_4$ as a minor, with distortion at most $14$, but the planar case remains unresolved.

record.title: Conjecture on equal orders of two random permutations
record.statement:
Let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be two independent uniformly random permutations in $S_k$, and write $|\sigma|$ and $|\tau|$ for their orders. **Equal-order conjecture.** There is a constant $K$ satisfying $W_1\leq K\leq 12$ such that

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(|\sigma|=|\tau|)=\frac{K}{k^2}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by experimental evidence and by lower bounds coming from conjugate permutations; the source does not provide a resolution, so it remains open.

record.title: Sullivant's secant–initial ideal conjecture for Plücker tree ideals
record.statement:
Let $d4b1$ be a binary phylogenetic $[n]$-tree, let $d714 d7d9 \in \mathbb{R}^{\binom{n}{2}}$ be a weight vector, and let $d70f \in \{\pm1\}^{\binom{n}{2}}$ be a sign vector such that

$$
J_{\mathcal{T}}=\tau\cdot \operatorname{in}_{\omega}(I_{2,n}).
$$

**Sullivant's conjecture.** For every $r$, one has

$$
\tau\cdot \operatorname{in}_{\omega}\left(I_{2,n}^{\{r\}}\right)=J_{\mathcal{T}}^{\{r\}}.
$$

The conjecture asks whether taking secant ideals commutes with taking the corresponding signed initial ideal for Plücker tree ideals. It is attributed in the source to Sullivant's Conjecture 7.10; no resolution is supplied here.

record.statement: Let $Q$ be a minimal mutation-infinite quiver. Let $\widehat{\Psi}(Q)$ denote the subgraph associated with quivers admitting maximal green sequences, as in Theorem~. **Minimal mutation-infinite quiver conjecture.** The results of Theorem~ hold for all minimal mutation-infinite quivers. The rank-four result is expected to extend to higher-rank minimal mutation-infinite quivers, but checking the quivers bounding the relevant component becomes substantially more difficult; the paper notes that even a rank-seven example requires checking at least 1200 quivers.

record.title: Homology decomposition conjecture for the two-term Yang–Baxter complex
record.statement:
Let $k=\mathbb{Q}[y,y^{-1}]$, let $V=k\{v_1,v_2\}$, and let $H_n$ denote the $n$-th homology group of the two-term Yang–Baxter chain complex associated with the displayed unital Yang–Baxter operator for $m=2$. Define $s_n=\sum_{i=1}^{n+1}f_i$, where $f_1=f_2=1$ and $(f_i)$ is the Fibonacci sequence, and define $a_n$ recursively by

$$
2^n=2+a_{n-1}+s_{n-2}+a_n+s_{n-1},\qquad a_1=0.
$$

**Homology decomposition conjecture.** For every $n$, 

$$
H_n\cong k^2\oplus\left(k/(1-y^2)\right)^{a_n}\oplus\left(k/(1-y^4)\right)^{s_{n-2}}.
$$

The formula was verified in the source for $n\leq 10$ and predicts the structure of the two-term Yang–Baxter homology in this family beyond the checked range.

record.title: The $h$-positivity conjecture for the symmetric function $\Psi_{21}$
record.statement:
Let $\alpha\in{\bf l}[n]$, and let $\Psi_{21}(\alpha)$ be the symmetric function defined by the coloring scheme whose monochromatic subsequences have standardization $2143\ldots(2a_i)(2a_i-1)$. Let ${\mathcal A}$ be a finite set of permutations, and call $\alpha$ **${\mathcal A}$-avoiding** when it avoids every permutation in ${\mathcal A}$. **The $h$-positivity conjecture.** There is a finite set of permutations ${\mathcal A}$ such that, for every $\mathcal A$-avoiding $\alpha\in{\bf l}[n]$, 

$$
(-1)^{n/2}\Psi_{21}(\alpha)(-h_1,-h_2,\ldots)
$$

is $h$-positive. The authors report that computer evidence suggests ${\mathcal A}=\emptyset$, but the existence of such a finite set and the asserted positivity are not established in the supplied text.

record.title: The hexagonal-grid realization conjecture for ball-packing contact numbers
record.statement:
Let $c(n)$ denote the maximal number of contacts among packings of $n$ congruent unit balls in the plane, where the balls are placed at vertices of a hexagonal grid. The exact maximal value of $c(n)$ is considered over all such grids.

**Hexagonal-grid realization conjecture.** The exact (maximal) value for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ can be achieved in some hexagonal grid.

Exact values are known for $n\leq 20$, and computations in the source support the claim for the values considered there, including examples with $n=14$ and $n=15$. The statement is presented as a conjecture for arbitrary $n$; its general status is not established by the supplied text.

record.title: Defect pattern conjecture for fourth-order Gaussian moment varieties
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_{n,4}$ be the Gaussian moment variety of order $4$ in $n$ variables, and let $\delta_j$ denote the defect of its $j$-th secant variety. The model-parameter count is compared with the ambient dimension $\binom{n+4}{4}-1$. **Fourth-order Gaussian defect conjecture.** The Gaussian moment variety $\mathcal{G}_{n,4}$ is $(n+3)$-defective with defect $\delta_{n+3}=1$ for $n\geq 8$. Furthermore, for all $r\geq 3$, the $(n+r)$-defect of $\mathcal{G}_{n,4}$ is

$$
\delta_{n+r}=\binom{r-1}{2},
$$

unless the number of model parameters exceeds the ambient dimension $\binom{n+4}{4}-1$. The pattern is supported by computations verified for $n\leq 14$, but no general proof is supplied.

record.title: Realization conjecture for all Conway and umbral twining functions
record.statement:
Let $N$ range over the 24 Niemeier lattices and let $\Phi(N)$ be the associated set of Conway or umbral twining functions. **Realization conjecture.** For every element $\phi\in\Phi(N)$, there exists a $K3$ nonlinear sigma model $\mathcal{T}$ with a symmetry $g$ such that

$$
\phi={\cal Z}_g(\mathcal{T}.)
$$

Thus every function produced by Conway or umbral moonshine should arise as a physical twining genus of a $K3$ nonlinear sigma model. The source presents this as a converse to the completeness conjecture; it remains unproved.
